paras: The Amazonian beardless tyrannulet (Camptostoma napaeum) is a small passerine bird in the tyrant flycatcher family Tyrannidae. It was formerly considered to be conspecific with southeastern beardless tyrannulet (Camptostoma obsoletum). It is found in the Amazon basin.

The Amazonian beardless tyrannulet was formally described in 1888 by the American ornithologist Robert Ridgway based on a specimen collected at Diamantina near Santarém on lower Amazon in Brazil. He coined the binomial name Ornithion napaeum where the specific epithet is from Ancient Greek ναπαιος/napaios meaning "of a wooded dell". This species was formerly considered to be a subspecies of the southeastern beardless tyrannulet (Camptostoma obsoletum) (then known as the southern beardless-tyrannulet). In 2026 it was elevated to species status based on differences in vocalization as well as minor differences in plumage.
C. n. napaeum (Ridgway, 1888) – far south-central Venezuela to the Guianas and northern Brazil (eastern Amazonas, Pará, and Amapá)
C. n. olivaceum (Berlepsch, 1889) – southeastern Colombia to eastern Ecuador, northeastern Peru, northern Bolivia, and western Brazil (western Amazonas)
